input.step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Nodes: kept all 12 whiteboard entities. The three Lambdas do different jobs (RaaS frontend, scaling calculator, spot-interruption handler) and the two SQS queues do different jobs (rendering requests vs. engine responses), so none were fused. The EC2 Auto Scaling box with the Spot icon is a single node for the rendering-engine fleet. 2) Flow 0 (render request): device -> API Gateway -> frontend Lambda -> request SQS -> rendering engines pull -> engines respond to the response SQS and upload segments to S3 -> the same Lambda invocation polls the response queue -> playlist returned to the device. The Lambda/response-queue edge follows the drawn arrow (Lambda -> top SQS) and is typed meta because the transcript says the Lambda pulls from that queue. 3) Flow 1 (playback): the player requests video segments from CloudFront, which pulls them from the S3 origin. 4) Flow 2 (spot interruption): a CloudWatch event notifies a Lambda that an instance is about to be reclaimed; the Lambda calls that instance's API to stop pulling and drain, then detaches it from the Auto Scaling group. 5) Flow 3 (scaling): rendering instances push CloudWatch metrics; Step Functions triggers a Lambda every 15 seconds; the Lambda consumes the metrics and tells the Auto Scaling group to increase in-service instances. The Lambda/CloudWatch edge follows the drawn arrow (Lambda -> CloudWatch) and is typed meta as a metric read. No components were added beyond the whiteboard and transcript.

graph.name: SundaySky: Rendering as a Service (RaaS) for Personalized Video on EC2 Spot
graph.notes: SundaySky's rendering-as-a-service ecosystem for personalized video. Generates billions of videos yearly and millions daily. Rendering runs entirely on EC2 Spot instances spread across multiple Availability Zones with diversified instance types for high availability. Custom scaling mechanism based on CloudWatch metrics, evaluated every 15 seconds via Step Functions and Lambda. Custom handling of the two-minute spot interruption notice via CloudWatch Events and Lambda. Planned next step: use Auto Scaling group instance weights to represent rendering capacity.

nodes.name: Phone or Computer
nodes.notes: Viewer's mobile or PC device with the video player. Opens a link to a personalized video (e.g. a monthly telco bill), receives a playlist, and requests video segments.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: First stop for rendering requests. Usage plans and API keys per customer are used to control the load on the rendering farm.

nodes.name: Lambda (RaaS Service Frontend)
nodes.notes: RaaS service frontend. Validates the rendering request, pushes rendering instructions to the request SQS queue, pulls the engine's response from the response SQS queue within the same invocation, and returns a link to a playlist file.

nodes.name: SQS (Rendering Request Queue)
nodes.notes: Bottom queue on the whiteboard. Holds rendering instructions; engine services pull rendering jobs from it when they have capacity.

nodes.name: SQS (Response Queue)
nodes.notes: Top queue on the whiteboard. The rendering engine responds here immediately so the response is as quick as possible; the same Lambda invocation pulls from it.

nodes.name: EC2 Auto Scaling (Spot Rendering Engines)
nodes.notes: Rendering engine service running entirely on EC2 Spot instances. Instances span multiple Availability Zones with diversified instance types for high availability. Instances push CloudWatch metrics. On spot interruption, an instance stops pulling from the queue, drains its current jobs (expected to finish within the two-minute notice), and is detached from the group.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores the video segments uploaded by the rendering engine; origin for CloudFront. The playlist file contains links to these segments.

nodes.name: CloudFront
nodes.notes: Serves video segments to the player, pulling them from the S3 origin.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Triggers the scaling Lambda function every 15 seconds.

nodes.name: Lambda (Scaling)
nodes.notes: Triggered by Step Functions every 15 seconds. Consumes CloudWatch metrics pushed by the rendering instances and, when higher traffic is expected, tells the Auto Scaling group to increase the number of in-service instances.

nodes.name: CloudWatch Events / Metrics
nodes.notes: Receives metrics pushed from the rendering instances. Emits a CloudWatch event when a specific spot instance ID is about to be reclaimed (two-minute interruption notice).

nodes.name: Lambda (Spot Interruption Handler)
nodes.notes: Invoked by a CloudWatch event carrying the instance ID about to be reclaimed. Calls that instance's API to stop pulling rendering requests and drain current jobs, then detaches the instance from the Auto Scaling group.

edges.notes: The viewer's device sends the rendering request to API Gateway.
API Gateway passes the request to the RaaS frontend Lambda.
After validation, the Lambda pushes rendering instructions to the request queue.
Rendering engines in the Auto Scaling group pull rendering jobs when they have capacity.
The rendering engine responds immediately to the response queue.
The rendering engine uploads video segments to S3.
The same Lambda invocation polls the response queue for the engine's response. Direction follows the drawn arrow.
The Lambda returns a link to the playlist file, which contains links to the video segments.
The player requests video segments through the CloudFront link.
CloudFront pulls the video segment from the S3 origin and plays it to the user.
A CloudWatch event notifies the Lambda that a specific spot instance ID is about to be reclaimed.
The Lambda calls the instance's API to stop pulling from the queue and drain current jobs, then detaches the instance from the Auto Scaling group.
Rendering instances push metrics to CloudWatch.
Step Functions triggers the scaling Lambda every 15 seconds.
The scaling Lambda consumes the CloudWatch metrics to calculate required capacity. Direction follows the drawn arrow.
When higher traffic is expected, the Lambda tells the Auto Scaling group to increase the number of in-service instances.
